summary.title: Dialect, High German and Swiss Standard German
points: Dialect is spoken with almost everyone; High German is for writing, news and school.
Swiss Standard German is High German with a Swiss accent and words like Velo.
Dialect has no lower status; using it signals closeness.
*rede* = speak; *am … lerne* = busy learning.

questions.explanation: Swiss accent and words like Velo and parkieren.

summary.title: Keeping people in dialect
points: Swiss people switch to High German to be polite when they hear an accent.
Ask kindly, once: *Chönd Si bitte Schwiizertüütsch rede?*
Say you understand more than you speak; answering in High German is fine.
*chli* = a bit; *Nöd so schnäll* = not so fast.

questions.prompt: What do you say (formal)?
options: Sprechen Sie bitte nur noch Hochdeutsch mit mir?

options: Schnäll, schnäll, bitte, mir händ Ziit.

options: A small child in the family

summary.title: The dialect map
points: Swiss German is a family of Alemannic dialects that differ in sounds, words and grammar.
Zurich German is spoken across most of the canton.
'Not': Zurich *nöd*, Bern *nid*, Basel *nit*.
*z Züri* = in or to Zurich; *schaffe* = work.

questions.prompt: How do you answer 'in Zurich'?
options: Ich arbeite in Zürich, wie alle.
Ich bi z Bärn am schaffe.

questions.prompt: Which dialect family is Swiss German part of?
questions.explanation: Alemannic also covers south-west Germany and Alsace.

summary.title: Writing without a standard
points: Swiss German has no official spelling; people write what they hear.
This course uses Dieth-style spelling: Huus, Ziit, guet, Wätter.
*sp* and *st* are written as in High German but said *schp* and *scht*.
Chats are often dialect; emails, letters and forms stay High German.

summary.title: Reading the pronunciation guide
points: Each card shows the Zurich spelling, a 'Say it' respelling and IPA.
CAPS = stressed syllable; doubled vowel = long.
*ie*, *ue*, *üe* glide; *ä* is open, *e* closed.
*ch* is always throaty; *b, d, g* are soft but voiceless; final *-n* drops.

points: Your ear is the gap, not your vocabulary.

summary.title: Where dialect fits
points: Dialect for speaking, High German for writing; Swiss Standard German in between.

Useful: *chli*, *nöd*, *z Züri*, *schaffe*.
